subject: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@signify.ai>, procure@signify.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable

Emily / Signify team — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short checklist we want to include in the MAP to remove friction during procurement and to validate the pilot during evaluation. Attaching a light tokenization model (unitization_token_model.csv) and a draft MAP workbook.

High-level asks: 
- Confirm target SLOs (p50/p95 latency) and max acceptable tokens per interaction for the pilot.
- Agree gating economics: tokens/$ threshold and acceptable 10% variance for the first 30 days.
- Approve the eval milestones and dates below (we propose 6-week pilot):
  - Week 0: provisioning + access + baseline embed tests
  - Week 2: quality checkpoints (sample prompts) + tokens/interaction sampling
  - Week 4: stress/batching runs and caching verification
  - Week 6: acceptance decision (go/no-go) and procurement signature

Important cost assumptions we used in the workbook: 
- Baseline tokens per response: 420 (mean).
- Caching reuse estimate: 18% of calls (prefix caching) for the core workflows.
- Batching policy: up to 8 concurrent requests per GPU slot during non-peak windows; expected 22% latency tail impact if batch size >4.

Please review and tell us which items you want to tighten/loosen. If this looks good, we'll fold the numbers into the MAP and add a DocuSign step for signature.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: unitization_token_model.csv, Signify_MAP_v1.xlsx
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@signify.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@signify.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable

Thanks Ava — this is helpful. Quick clarifying Qs before we circulate internally to procurement: 
1) Baseline tokens per response: is 420 an average across all templates or the support/FAQ flow? We have high-variance prompts.
2) Caching: 18% sounds reasonable for our FAQ caching, but can you show sensitivity if caching is only 8%?
3) Batching: our security team is concerned about latency tail when batching >4 — can you propose a fallback (smaller batch / autoscale spike) as a gating item?

Procurement asked for a single-sheet summary they can attach to the PO. Can you produce a one-page cost summary (tokens/$ at 3 usage scenarios: 50k, 250k, 1M interactions) with clear assumptions?

If we can get that by EOD Mon (their deadline), procurement will fast-track the legal review.

— Emily
Director of AI Integrations | Signify AI
emily.torres@signify.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@signify.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable

Emily — quick simulation notes (internal assumptions first, then answers):

Assumptions used in the workbook (explainers):
- tokenization: all inputs + outputs counted; mean payload = 420 tokens (median 380, 90th 940) across sampled templates from Signify test corpus.
- caching: prefix-level reuse of top-25 intents; baseline 18% reuse; low-case 8% scenario included below.
- batching: two modes simulated: responsive (batch size <=3 target p95 latency <450ms) and throughput (batch size up to 8, p95 increases ~220ms).
- cost model: hosted pricing model with per-1k-token price tiers, plus estimated infra uplift for burst autoscale (10% of monthly usage).

Sensitivity (summary numbers):
- Scenario A (conservative): 50k interactions/month, tokens/interaction=420, caching=8% => ~20M tokens/mo => $X (see attachment) => tokens/$ ~20,000 tokens per dollar.
- Scenario B (typical): 250k interactions/mo, caching=18% => ~95M tokens/mo => tokens/$ ~85,000 tokens per dollar (with batching savings).
- Scenario C (peak): 1M interactions/mo, caching=18%, heavy batching => ~360M tokens/mo => tokens/$ ~130,000 tokens per dollar (batching/prefetch efficiency).

Proposed gating fallback: if observed p95 latency > target by >15% during week-4 stress runs, we automatically switch to "responsive" batching and add 1x burst capacity for peak windows. This should keep tail latency within SLO, at a predicted 6-9% incremental cost. Include as MAP clause?

Action items for Ava/Jordan: I can convert these sims into a single-page procurement summary and a short appendix showing 8% vs 18% caching. ETA: Mon EOD.

Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@signify.ai>, procure@signify.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable

Emily / procurement — attaching the one-page procurement summary (Signify_MAP_v1.xlsx, first tab: \"Procurement Summary\"). Highlights called out in the MAP: 
- Three usage scenarios with tokens/$ and monthly $ estimate (conservative/expected/peak).
- Gating: Week-4 stress test p95 latency must be within 15% of target or Redwood will execute the responsive batching fallback and absorb the first-week burst cost up to $2k while we tune.
- Evaluation acceptance criteria: accuracy/quality pass rate >= 88% on the provided sample prompts, tokens/interaction average within +/-15% of modeled expectation, and no security compliance blockers.

Proposed close timetable (we set dates to align with your procurement window):
- 09/08: Redwood delivers final MAP workbook + procurement summary (this file).
- 09/10: Signify legal review complete (target).
- 09/14: DocuSign link issued; signature target by 09/21.

If procurement signs off on the one-pager, we can mark week-0 provisioning to start 48 hours after signature. Jordan — will you draft the DocuSign envelope when we have the final SOW?

Next steps for Signify: please confirm the caching sensitivity threshold you prefer (8% or 18%) and whether the responsive-batching fallback clause is acceptable. Procurement: does the single-sheet summary meet your requirement?

Thanks,
Ava
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@signify.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@signify.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — Unit economics sanity checks & close timetable

Thanks — LGTM on the one-pager and the gating language. Procurement confirms the single-sheet summary is sufficient for their PO attachment. 

Quick notes: 
- Signify prefers the conservative caching assumption for the PO (8%). We'll run the internal caching instrumentation during week-2 and update the MAP if we see higher reuse.
- The responsive-batching fallback clause is fine, but procurement asks that the first-week burst cost cap be changed from $2k to $3k. Can Redwood accept that as a limit?

If Redwood agrees, procurement will move to legal review and we expect to complete signatures by 09/20. Please add a DocuSign step and send the envelope when the SOW is finalized.

— Emily
